insight: For New Zealand in the 2026 World Cup, hydration breaks have had a mixed impact on their performance. When they were pressing before a break, they tended to lose momentum, with their average change in momentum being -0.100 per minute, and they were only able to maintain their momentum once out of three times. In contrast, when they weren't pressing before a break, they actually gained momentum on average, with a change of +0.033 per minute, suggesting that the breaks gave them a chance to regroup and refocus. Overall, New Zealand gained momentum after a hydration break in half of the instances, with an average change of -0.033 per minute across all six breaks, indicating that the breaks had a slightly negative but relatively minor impact on their overall performance.
